incident: A Truly Graceful Wipe Out (Truebot/FlawedGrace to MBR Killer wiper in 29 hours)

sources.title: A Truly Graceful Wipe Out - The DFIR Report (2023-06-12)
sources.what_it_gave: entry (404 TDS email drive-by -> Truebot Document_may_24_16654.exe), hops (pass-the-hash atexec, CS jump psexec every 5-20 min, FlawedGrace on all hosts), cred access (registry-hive remote dump ~secretsdump, LSASS, PtH), exfil (observed, tool not named), impact (MBR Killer wiper on all FlawedGrace hosts incl file server), 29h

narrative_before: In a May 2023 intrusion the DFIR Report observed Truebot delivered via the '404 TDS' email-to-drive-by chain (Document_may_24_16654.exe, a fake Adobe doc) on the beachhead host. Truebot loaded FlawedGrace, which abused the Print Spooler service's RequiredPrivileges registry key to escalate and persist, disabled Defender real-time monitoring, created and removed a temporary local admin for failed tunneled-RDP attempts, and did domain-admin/DC discovery. ~1h in, a remote registry-hive credential dump (resembling an older Impacket secretsdump) ran. ~2h in Truebot loaded Cobalt Strike; ~4h in the actors ran net/nltest/AdFind discovery, accessed LSASS on the beachhead, and used a local administrator hash for pass-the-hash lateral movement. They used Impacket atexec for remote discovery and Cobalt Strike jump psexec to move to a new host every 5-20 minutes, loading FlawedGrace on each. After a lull, ~17h later they returned, enumerated shares and exfiltrated data. ~4h after exfil began, merely 29h in, they deployed the MBR Killer wiper on all FlawedGrace hosts including a file server, overwriting the MBR and rebooting hosts to an inoperable boot screen. No ransom note was left.

detection_moments.description: Truebot/FlawedGrace on the beachhead (404 TDS drive-by); spooler-based priv-esc; ~1h in a remote registry-hive credential dump.
detection_moments.evidence: 'delivering the initial Truebot payload Document_may_24_16654.exe ... using a remote dumping tool to extract credentials via the registry hives ... resemble those of secretsdump' - A Truly Graceful Wipe Out, The DFIR Report

detection_moments.description: ~4-5h: LSASS on beachhead; local-admin hash pass-the-hash; atexec remote discovery; CS jump psexec to a new host every 5-20 min, FlawedGrace loaded on each.
detection_moments.evidence: 'leveraged a local administrator hash to perform pass-the-hash lateral movement ... used Cobalt Strike's jump psexec module to further move between hosts ... moving to a new system every 5-20 minutes' - A Truly Graceful Wipe Out

detection_moments.description: ~29h: after share enumeration and data exfiltration, the MBR Killer wiper is deployed on all FlawedGrace hosts incl a file server, overwriting MBRs and rebooting to an inoperable state.
detection_moments.evidence: 'the threat actors deployed the MBR Killer wiper on all hosts where FlawedGrace had been running, including a file server. This executable overwrote the MBR ... rendering the hosts unusable' - A Truly Graceful Wipe Out

attack_path: pass-the-hash with a local admin hash + Cobalt Strike jump psexec (T1550.002/T1021.002)
Impacket atexec remote discovery and FlawedGrace loaded (T1053.005)
MBR Killer wiper deployed on all FlawedGrace hosts incl the file server (T1561.002)
ambiguities: Hosts named by role only; victim sector not stated. Count of hosts moved to not given; modelled as srv_1/srv_2/pc_2/pc_3 plus the file server.
Exfil tool not named; data exfiltrated but content/volume not quantified.
This is a wiper (MBR Killer), not ransomware; no ransom note / extortion was found.
Moments are the report's own timeline markers (initial, PtH/lateral, wipe), not a defender detection timeline.
